subject: English
passage:
[Table 1]

One measure of a nation's commitment to clean energy is the amount its government spends annually on renewable energy subsidies. A student writing a report on energy policy in several European countries notes that among the countries in the table, most had annual increases in renewable energy subsidy spending in 2020 and 2021, but that trend wasn't universal. For example, ______
prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?

choices.A: in each year shown, spending on fossil fuel subsidies in those countries was greater than spending on renewable energy subsidies.
choices.B: Germany's renewable energy subsidy spending was higher in 2019 than it was in 2021.
choices.C: Spain's annual renewable energy subsidy spending decreased from 2019 to 2020.
choices.D: in each year shown, Germany had higher renewable energy subsidy spending than any of the other countries.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text, providing an example that illustrates that the annual increases in renewable energy subsidy spending in 2020 and 2021 weren't universal. According to the table, Spain's annual spending on renewable energy subsidies was $14.2 billion in 2019 and then decreased to $11.6 billion in 2020. This decrease shows that not all of the countries included in the table saw increases in annual renewable energy subsidy spending in 2020.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the table doesn't provide any data regarding spending on fossil fuel subsidies. Even if that data were provided, it wouldn't be relevant to the claim that the trend of annual increases in renewable energy subsidy spending in 2020 and 2021 was not universal.
